one_fix: After the comparison's closing line 'Manual review still suits patients who cannot complete the scan.' insert a button 'See the order flow in the demo' to #demo. This breaks the roughly 3,460 px stretch with no call to action across the comparison and accuracy blocks.

points_lost.Proof of belonging to the vertical: The three steps never name the pharmacy's own systems (PMR or prescriber dashboard, order management). There is no MHRA or CQC context. There is no vertical figure, only the waiver substitutes and an unnamed 'including an online pharmacy'. A page with areaServed=UK shows only USD prices.
points_lost.Claims discipline: BMI is never expanded (M1). The manual-evidence column describes video consultations and clinical records as photos 'sent by the patient, with little record of when they were taken'. 'Body metrics' is an off-canon term. The page never says whether the Smart Scales estimate itself uses the height the patient supplied, which bears directly on 'a second weight source' and 'a route other than the patient's own answers'.
points_lost.Sales argument: The H1 outcome ('a live weight check') is what FitXpress returns, not what the pharmacy pays for (defensible, inspection-ready prescribing). The hero lede describes the process, which slot 3 forbids. No pharmacy outcome is stated, even hedged. The pricing lines have no conclusion. At 1,592 words the page sits at the top of the budget.
points_lost.Uniqueness against the parent: It overlaps /for-bmi-verification/ (same buyer, same feature) and the hub compliance guide's GPhC framing. The data, accuracy, pricing and pilot blocks are largely template text shared with the fitness and insurance pages, so the 60% rule cannot be confirmed.
points_lost.Conversion: There are about 3,460 px (more than four desktop screens) with no button across the comparison and accuracy blocks, which breaks 'a CTA every second screen'. The events have not been fired. The hero anchors to #form, with #demo only as an alias.
points_lost.Copy in the buyer's language: GPhC and buyers say 'BMI verification', but the page coins 'weight check'. 'Declared weight', 'self-reported weight' and 'the patient's own answers' are used interchangeably. US spelling is used for UK buyers. One FAQ answer opens with a subjectless fragment ('As one step the pharmacy configures.').
points_lost.Human copy: The scan-record bullets and step 2 all end in the same participial benefit tail ('giving…', 'pointing…', 'sparing…' three times), so that section reads as a filled template. An opinion and a boundary are present ('the evidence belongs with the order', 'It can.').
points_lost.Search and AI visibility: No FAQ question covers integration or links to the API documentation (a kit requirement). Two FAQs restate the body: the video-consultation fallback and 'the pilot measures the effect'. The focus keyphrase is a coined phrase, while 'online pharmacy BMI verification' is absent from the H1 and the H2s. GEO phrases from the keyword map are not evident.
points_lost.Place in the site and technical layer: There is only one sibling vertical (telehealth); BMI verification is a feature page, and neither fitness nor insurance is linked. There is no link up (justified while the parent redirects). Performance has not been measured, no full keyboard tab-through was done, and 1440 px was not checked.
